clues: This city stands by the Ravi River in east Punjab, in Pakistan. It is the proud heart of the whole Punjab region.
Hot summer days come first, then the rains crash down. From late June, monsoon storms bring floods, and thick fog fills cold winter days.
In 1849, troops of a British trade firm took this city. It then became the capital of Punjab under British rule.
Book fans know this city well. It holds a world mark as a City of Literature for its strong book trade.
Its great old fort and the famed Shalimar Gardens are both world heritage sites. See that pair, and the answer is clear.
